# /generate-pages

## Purpose

Turn planned pages into rendered candidates. Pages are generated in reading
order, one at a time, because each reviewed page becomes a spatial
reference for the next and a defect that slips through is copied forward.
Every returned image is saved as a new version, opened, and recorded with
whatever provenance the tool reports. The command ends with candidates. It
does not decide whether they are good; `/visual-review` does that on the
pixels.

## Use When

- Pages have reference plans, the ledger audit reports zero errors, and the
  masters they use are approved.
- A page's plan or references were corrected after the repair limit was
  reached, and the page starts again as a first render of the revised plan.
- You want the cost estimate and the handoff packages for an issue before
  committing to anything (dry run).

## Inputs

- `issue` (ID, required unless `page` is given): the `ISS_###` to generate.
- `page` (ID or range, optional): a single `PG_###_###` or a range such as
  `PG_001_003..PG_001_006`; default is every page of the issue without a
  reviewed render, in reading order.
- `provider` (string, optional, default `generation.provider` of the page,
  then `default_providers.image` in `project.yaml`): an ID from
  `manifests/image-providers.json`.
- `--dry-run` (flag, default on): write request specs and pending records;
  call nothing.
- `--live` (flag, optional, default off): call the provider, after the cost
  confirmation.

## Invokes Agents

- image-generation-specialist
- prompt-director

## Required Skills

- image-generation
- prompt-compilation
- reference-selection

## Process

1. Check the preconditions for the batch and stop on the first that fails.
   No `open_questions` entry with `blocking: true` lacks a `resolution`.
   `node scripts/check-continuity.js --root production --issue <ISS_ID>`
   reports zero errors. Every page has a `reference-plan.yaml`, and every
   asset in it is `approved` in the manifest. Nothing is generated from a
   freehand prompt.
2. Cost gate. Estimate the batch (pages x provider rate), list the pages,
   and wait for an explicit confirmation. One confirmation covers exactly
   the batch shown; more pages, another provider, or a repair run is a new
   batch. For the estimate and the handoff packages of a whole issue, run
   `node scripts/generate-assets.js --issue production/issues/<ISS_ID>
   --provider <id>`, which is a dry run.
3. Take the pages one at a time along the `continuity.enters_from` and
   `exits_to` chain. Do not request page N+1 until page N's render has been
   opened and reviewed.
4. For the page in hand, confirm its reference plan is current. If the
   previous page has been reviewed since the plan was written, run `node
   scripts/build-reference-plan.js --page <page.yaml> --provider <id>` so
   that render is attached as `spatial_continuity`. An unreviewed previous
   page is never attached.
5. prompt-director compiles the package: `node scripts/compile-prompts.js
   --page <page.yaml> --provider <id>`. Read it before sending. The style
   block is verbatim and the look master is attached with role `style`.
   The differences between adjacent characters are stated in words. In
   `in_image` mode `lettering_text` lists every string exactly; in
   `overlay` mode the prompt asks for art without text. `source_hashes`
   match the current files. Set the page's `status` to `prompted`.
6. Generate. Run `node scripts/generate-assets.js --page <page.yaml>
   --provider <id>` for the dry run, and add `--live --yes` after the
   confirmation from step 2. With `harness-native` or `manual` the script
   writes a handoff package; the harness image tool or a person produces
   the image from it.
7. Save the returned image as the next free version,
   `renders/<PG_ID>_V##.png` (or `.jpg`). Never write over an existing
   version and never reuse a number.
8. Complete the generation record under `production/generations/<PG_ID>/`:
   `provider`, `prompt_package`, `output_render`, `media_files`, `status`.
   Record what the tool reported and nothing else. An unreported model is
   the literal `unreported`. An unreported cost is `amount: null` with
   `reported: false`. An unreported seed is `null`. List each of them in
   `metadata_unavailable`.
9. Open the saved file and look at it before using it for anything: the
   right page, the planned panel count, the cast present, lettering present
   or absent according to the mode. A successful call means an image
   exists. It is not a quality pass. Set `status: rendered`, and set
   `current_render` if the page had none; a page that already stands on a
   reviewed render keeps it until the new version is reviewed. From the
   first render of an issue, its `status` is `production`.
10. Hand the render to `/visual-review`, run by a reviewer who did not
    generate it. On `pass` or `fixed`, go to the next page. On `flagged`,
    stop the sequence and go to `/repair-page`: a flagged page is never
    attached to the next request "for now".
11. Run the self-evaluation gates on the records and page files this run
    wrote, then report the batch in two separate parts. Mechanical: files
    saved, records valid, spend against estimate, metadata unavailable.
    Visual: which renders have been reviewed and with what verdict, and
    which are still candidates.

## Outputs

- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/renders/<PG_ID>_V##.png`,
  versioned candidates, never overwritten.
- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/prompts/<provider>.yaml`,
  validates against `schemas/prompt-package.schema.json`.
- `production/generations/<PG_ID>/GEN_<PG_ID>_<attempt##>.yaml`, one per
  request, dry runs included; validates against
  `schemas/generation-record.schema.json`.
- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/page.yaml`, with `status` and
  `current_render` updated (`schemas/page.schema.json`).

## Notes

- Cost warning: this command can spend money. Dry run is the default, the
  estimate is always shown first, and the hook `require-cost-confirmation.js`
  blocks `generate-assets --live` without `--yes`.
- `--issue` is for dry runs. It is not a way to render an issue unattended;
  live requests go page by page.
- Several candidates of the same page may be requested when their cost was
  confirmed. Each gets its own version and record, and one is chosen at
  review.
- `generation.mode: per_panel` generates each panel as a working image.
  The page still ends as one render with one `<PG_ID>_V##` ID, assembled in
  an image tool to the layout in `page.yaml` and noted in the record's
  `response.summary`. The review is of the assembled page.
- Format differences: a webtoon page is one scroll segment with the
  segment's aspect ratio from `project.yaml`. Check the provider supports
  that ratio before the batch.
- Never edit a returned image by hand and keep its version. A change is a
  new version through `/repair-page`, so provenance stays true.
- Related: `/reference-plan` and `/smart-page` (before), `/visual-review`
  (after every page), `/repair-page` (flagged pages), `/lettering` (overlay
  mode).
